tables.comment: One thing that happened, as a browser or the app reported it.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: What happened, such as `signup` or `clicked_buy`.

columns.name: distinct_id
columns.comment: Who it happened to: an id the browser keeps, not an account.

columns.name: properties
columns.comment: The event's properties, as a JSON object of strings.

tables.comment: `live.changes`: one row per written row of a live table.

columns.name: seq
columns.comment: The change's place among the database's changes.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment: The Postgres transaction that wrote it, which joins it to its commit.

columns.name: version
columns.comment: SQLite: the commit's version, set just before the commit.

columns.name: table_name
columns.comment: The changed table, with its namespace: `messages` or `billing.invoices`.

columns.name: op
columns.comment: What the write did.

columns.name: key
columns.comment: The changed row's key, in key column order.

columns.name: old
columns.comment:
The row before an update or delete, without `secret` and
`live = skip` columns.

columns.name: new
columns.comment: The row after an insert or update, without those columns.

columns.name: changed
columns.comment: For an update, every column whose value changed; empty otherwise.

tables.comment:
`live.commits`: one row per committed transaction that wrote a live
table.

columns.name: version
columns.comment:
The transaction's place in the version line. Gaps are transactions
that rolled back after taking a version, which never become visible.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment:
The Postgres transaction ID, which joins the commit to its changes.
`None` on SQLite.

columns.name: committed_at
columns.comment: When the transaction committed.

columns.name: actor
columns.comment: Who made the change, when the transaction said.

columns.name: origin
columns.comment:
What made it: what the transaction said, such as an operation's
name, or `sql`.

columns.name: lsn
columns.comment:
Replication capture: where the commit's record starts in Postgres's
write-ahead log, which orders commits as the database committed them.
`None` for commits captured by triggers.

tables.comment:
`live.pending`, Postgres only: the transactions waiting for a version at
commit.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment: The transaction's ID.

columns.name: account
columns.comment: Whose notice it is: their account's UUID.

columns.name: action
columns.comment: The button on it.

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: `info`, `success`, `warning`, or `error`.

columns.name: read_at
columns.comment: When its owner read it.

tables.comment:
One enqueued job, in the `rpc` pack's `jobs` table.

It's a live table: a client follows a job with
[`use_job`](crate::client::use_job), and the hub sends each change. Its
policies show a job to the account that enqueued it, and to whoever
`#[rpc::job(visible_to = ...)]` names, and let only the owner change it.

columns.name: key
columns.comment:
The app's idempotency key, if it gave one: enqueuing it again returns
the same job, until the job is pruned.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The job's name.

columns.name: queue
columns.comment: Its queue.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment: The arguments, as JSON.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
The account that enqueued it, as a UUID, or empty when nobody signed
in did.

columns.name: viewer
columns.comment:
Another account that may read it, from `visible_to = argument`, or
empty.

columns.name: visibility
columns.comment: Who else may read it.

columns.name: serial_key
columns.comment:
The job's name and its `serialize_by` argument: at most one job with
a key runs at a time.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: How many times a worker has started it.

columns.name: max_attempts
columns.comment: How many starts it gets before it fails.

columns.name: priority
columns.comment: Higher runs first.

columns.name: run_at
columns.comment: Not before this instant.

columns.name: deadline_at
columns.comment: No attempt starts after this instant.

columns.name: started_at
columns.comment: When a worker last started it.

columns.name: finished_at
columns.comment: When it reached `done`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.

columns.name: locked_until
columns.comment: Until when the running worker holds it; `None` when no one does.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the body returned, as JSON.

columns.name: error
columns.comment: Why the last attempt failed.

columns.name: progress
columns.comment: What it last said it was doing.

columns.name: fraction
columns.comment: How far along it last said it was, from 0 to 1.

columns.name: steps
columns.comment: The results of the steps it finished, by name.

columns.name: cancel_requested
columns.comment: Someone asked it to stop.

columns.name: failure_pending
columns.comment: It failed, and its `on_failure` mutation hasn't run yet.

tables.comment:
One mutation call that ran with a request ID, and what it returned.

Each caller sees only their own receipts: the policy compares
[`owner`](Self::owner) with the [`ReceiptOwner`] the RPC adds to the
context it runs a mutation in.

columns.name: owner
columns.comment:
Who called: their [`Identity::caller`](super::Identity::caller), such
as a session ID, or [`ANONYMOUS`] for anonymous callers.

columns.name: request_id
columns.comment: The ID the call came with.

columns.name: operation
columns.comment: The operation's name.

columns.name: arguments
columns.comment:
A SHA-256 of the operation's name and arguments, in hex: a repeat
with the same request ID and other arguments is refused rather than
answered with another call's result.

columns.name: result
columns.comment: What the call returned, as JSON.
